requirements.quote:
receipt of a packet protected with
   Handshake keys confirms that the peer successfully processed an
   Initial packet.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a packet protected with Handshake keys.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the receipt as confirmation that the peer successfully processed an Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a valid Handshake-key-protected packet and inspect whether Initial-packet processing by the peer is treated as confirmed.

requirements.quote:
Once an endpoint has successfully processed a
   Handshake packet from the peer, it can consider the peer address to
   have been validated.
requirements.condition: An endpoint has successfully processed a Handshake packet from its peer.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may transition the peer address to validated.
requirements.why_checkable: The address-validation state can be inspected after successful processing of a peer Handshake packet.

requirements.quote:
an endpoint MAY consider the peer address validated if
   the peer uses a connection ID chosen by the endpoint and the
   connection ID contains at least 64 bits of entropy.
requirements.condition: The peer uses a connection ID chosen by the endpoint, and that connection ID contains at least 64 bits of entropy.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may consider the peer address validated.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can vary connection-ID provenance and entropy and inspect the resulting address-validation state.

requirements.quote:
For the client, the value of the Destination Connection ID field in
   its first Initial packet allows it to validate the server address as
   a part of successfully processing any packet.
requirements.condition: A client successfully processes a packet whose authenticity or server possession is established using the Destination Connection ID from the client's first Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow the client to validate the server address as part of processing that packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can correlate the first Initial Destination Connection ID with processed server packets and inspect server-address validation state.

requirements.quote:
Initial packets from
   the server are protected with keys that are derived from this value
requirements.condition: The server sends Initial packets in response to the client's first Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Protect the server Initial packets with keys derived from the Destination Connection ID value in the client's first Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet protection keys can be derived from the recorded Destination Connection ID and used to verify the server Initial packets.

requirements.quote:
Alternatively, the value is echoed
   by the server in Version Negotiation packets (Section 6) or included
   in the Integrity Tag in Retry packets (Section 5.8 of [QUIC-TLS]).
requirements.condition: The server sends a Version Negotiation or Retry packet as the alternative proof based on the client's first Initial Destination Connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Echo the value in a Version Negotiation packet, or include it in the Integrity Tag of a Retry packet, according to the packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: The fields and integrity input of Version Negotiation and Retry packets can be decoded and compared with the first Initial Destination Connection ID.

requirements.quote:
Prior to validating the client address, servers MUST NOT send more
   than three times as many bytes as the number of bytes they have
   received.
requirements.condition: A server has not yet validated the client address.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit bytes sent to no more than three times the number of bytes received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending more than three times the number of bytes received before validating the client address.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can track received and transmitted byte totals before validation and verify the 3:1 bound.

requirements.quote:
For the purposes of
   avoiding amplification prior to address validation, servers MUST
   count all of the payload bytes received in datagrams that are
   uniquely attributed to a single connection.
requirements.condition: A server computes the received-byte allowance before address validation for datagrams uniquely attributable to one connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Count all payload bytes received in those datagrams.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omitting any received payload bytes from uniquely attributable datagrams when computing the anti-amplification allowance.
requirements.why_checkable: Datagram payload lengths and connection attribution can be recorded and compared with the server's anti-amplification accounting.

requirements.quote:
This includes datagrams
   that contain packets that are successfully processed and datagrams
   that contain packets that are all discarded.
requirements.condition: A received datagram is uniquely attributed to one connection and its packets are successfully processed or all discarded.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the datagram's payload bytes in received-byte accounting in either case.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Excluding a uniquely attributable datagram merely because all of its packets were discarded.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can send both processable and wholly discarded packets in attributable datagrams and inspect the accounting total.

requirements.quote:
Clients MUST ensure that UDP datagrams containing Initial packets
   have UDP payloads of at least 1200 bytes, adding PADDING frames as
   necessary.
requirements.condition: A client sends a UDP datagram containing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the UDP payload is at least 1200 bytes, adding PADDING frames when necessary to reach that size.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending a UDP datagram containing an Initial packet with a UDP payload smaller than 1200 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted datagram's UDP payload length and any PADDING frames can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
To
   prevent this deadlock, clients MUST send a packet on a Probe Timeout
   (PTO); see Section 6.2 of [QUIC-RECOVERY].
requirements.condition: A client's Probe Timeout fires during connection establishment.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a packet on the Probe Timeout.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allowing the Probe Timeout to expire without sending a packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A controlled PTO event can be triggered and outbound packet emission observed.

requirements.quote:
the client
   MUST send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram that contains at least
   1200 bytes if it does not have Handshake keys
requirements.condition: A client must send on a Probe Timeout and does not have Handshake keys.
requirements.required_behavior: Send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram containing at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending only a non-Initial packet or using a UDP datagram smaller than 1200 bytes in this PTO branch.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can fire a PTO before Handshake keys exist and inspect the packet type and datagram size.

requirements.quote:
and otherwise send a
   Handshake packet.
requirements.condition: A client must send on a Probe Timeout and has Handshake keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Failing to send a Handshake packet in this PTO branch.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can fire a PTO after Handshake keys become available and inspect the emitted packet type.

requirements.quote:
QUIC uses a token in the Initial packet
   to provide address validation prior to completing the handshake.
requirements.condition: Client-address validation is performed before completion of the handshake using this token mechanism.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the address-validation token in the Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The Initial packet can be decoded to verify the presence and placement of the token used for pre-handshake validation.

requirements.quote:
This token is delivered to the client during connection establishment
   with a Retry packet (see Section 8.1.2) or in a previous connection
   using the NEW_TOKEN frame (see Section 8.1.3).
requirements.condition: A client supplies a token for address validation in an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a token delivered either by a Retry packet during the current connection establishment or by a NEW_TOKEN frame in a previous connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Token provenance can be recorded and checked against prior Retry packets or NEW_TOKEN frames.

requirements.quote:
servers are also constrained in what they can send by the limits set
   by the congestion controller.
requirements.condition: A server sends data, including before address validation.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep server transmissions within the limits set by the congestion controller in addition to applicable pre-validation sending limits.
requirements.why_checkable: Server transmissions can be compared with the active congestion controller's current sending allowance.

requirements.quote:
Clients are only constrained by the
   congestion controller.
requirements.condition: A client determines its sending limit under the constraints discussed in this passage.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the congestion controller's sending constraint.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Applying the server's pre-address-validation anti-amplification sending limit to the client.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect whether client sending is governed by congestion control without imposing the server-only anti-amplification limit.
